title: Korea's Exports Top $800 Billion for the First Time, Eyeing a $1 Trillion Year
content:
Korea Macro Brief · October 1, 2026

Korea's cumulative exports topped $800 billion for the first time ever in September, surpassing all of last year's full-year total in just nine months, as semiconductor exports crossed $60 billion in a single month for the first time. Here is what's driving the record and what the government says could still get in the way of a $1 trillion year.

MetricSeptember 2026Change
Monthly exports$120.94 billion+83.5% YoY, first time above $120B
Jan–Sep cumulative exports$814.5 billion+56.8% YoY, already above all of 2025 ($709.3B)
Semiconductor exports$60.3 billion+262.8% YoY, first time above $60B; 49.9% of total exports
Trade surplus$49.85 billionRecord monthly high; 20th straight month of surplus

What the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy reported

  • September exports hit $120.94 billion, an all-time monthly record, up 83.5% from a year earlier — achieved despite 2.5 fewer working days than last September due to the Chuseok holiday. Daily average exports rose 104.9% to $5.63 billion, topping $5 billion for the first time.
  • Cumulative exports for January through September reached $814.5 billion, up 56.8% year over year, already exceeding 2025's full-year record of $709.3 billion. Korea needs about $185.5 billion more to reach $1 trillion for the year.
  • Memory chip exports alone surged 358.6% to $54.07 billion, driven by AI data center demand and rising memory prices.
  • Non-semiconductor exports also rose 23%, with 11 of the 20 major export categories growing.

Other categories that set records

Computer exports (mainly enterprise SSDs) jumped 435.3% to $7 billion, an all-time high, on AI infrastructure demand. Cosmetics exports rose 31.4% to $1.51 billion, also a record, with electrical equipment up 23.4% to $1.83 billion. Ship exports rose 29.9% to $3.76 billion on higher-value LNG carrier deliveries. Wireless device exports rose 23.4% to $2.14 billion, extending an 11-month growth streak. (Reported, government data)

Automobile exports fell 5.5% to $6.05 billion on fewer working days and weak used-car exports; general machinery, bio-health and agri-food exports also declined.

By destination

Exports to China rose 122.7% to $26.01 billion, topping $20 billion for a fourth straight month on semiconductor, wireless device and computer demand. Exports to the U.S. rose 137.0% to $24.33 billion, a 10th straight month of growth. ASEAN exports rose 92.6% to $21.29 billion, topping $20 billion in a month for the first time. EU exports rose 20.9% to $8.65 billion. Middle East exports fell 14.1% to $1.6 billion on Strait of Hormuz transit difficulties.

What could still derail a $1 trillion year

Trade Minister Kim Jung-kwan said a $1 trillion export year is within reach but that "intensifying global protectionism and Middle East tensions remain major variables," and pledged to keep high-level trade channels open with major partners to monitor export restrictions and respond preemptively through year-end. (Reported)

Quick FAQ

Has Korea already hit $1 trillion in exports this year?
No. Nine-month cumulative exports are $814.5 billion; roughly $185.5 billion more is needed to reach $1 trillion by year-end.

What's driving the semiconductor export surge?
AI data center demand, rising memory chip prices, and an end-of-quarter effect, per the ministry; memory chips alone rose 358.6% year over year.

Did every export category grow?
No. Automobiles, general machinery, bio-health and agri-food exports all declined in September, mainly on fewer working days from the Chuseok holiday and sector-specific softness.
